title: Tri-Finger Robot Arm
headline: Deep reinforcement learning for visual pick-and-place manipulation
summary: This project compares A2C, DQN, PPO, and SAC for Kuka pick-and-place manipulation in PyBullet. The agents learn from 48 by 48 RGB observations and are evaluated around sample efficiency, policy stability, and task completion.
problem: Vision-based robotic manipulation couples sparse task rewards with high-dimensional observations, making it difficult to learn stable and sample-efficient grasping policies.
contribution: A comparative implementation and evaluation of four deep reinforcement learning families on a shared Kuka grasping environment, spanning value-based, actor-critic, and off-policy methods.
pipeline: Observe the simulated Kuka workspace through RGB frames.
Select among seven discrete end-effector actions.
Train A2C, DQN, PPO, and SAC policies under a shared grasping objective.
Compare learning behavior, stability, and successful object lifts.
evidence: Algorithm implementations and saved policy checkpoints for A2C, DQN, PPO, and SAC.
Animated Kuka grasping artifact and experiment visualizations.
A detailed project article covering the literature, methods, experiments, and results.
limitations: The project uses a simulated Kuka environment and a constrained action space. Results do not establish transfer to physical hardware or unconstrained manipulation.
